articles.title: Former IAF Group Captain Abhinandan Varthaman joins Fly91 as pilot: A look at his education and training
articles.summary: News News: \"We do not rise to the level of our expectations,\" the old military aphorism goes, \"we fall to the level of our training.\" Group Captain Abhinandan Va.
articles.body: "We do not rise to the level of our expectations," the old military aphorism goes, "we fall to the level of our training." Group Captain Abhinandan Varthaman, one of the most photographed officers in the Indian Air Force (IAF), has spent 22 years proving the second half of that sentence, even as the country mythologised him for a single evening in February 2019.Varthaman has taken premature retirement from the IAF and joined Goa based regional carrier Fly91 as a commercial pilot. He left the force on March 31 and is reported to have joined the airline in August, where he is currently undergoing type training on the ATR 72-600 turboprop before he can fly commercial routes such as Goa-Hyderabad. Fly91 has confirmed his association with the airline but declined to share further details, saying information about individual employees is a private matter. Varthaman himself, true to form, has said nothing.The moustache, the "Sir, I am fine" answer to his interrogators, the F-16 he brought down before ejecting into hostile territory: all of it made for gripping television. What made for less compelling television, and therefore received far less attention, was the seventeen years of unglamorous preparation that came before it.A cantonment childhoodVarthaman was born on June 21, 1983 in Chennai to a Tamil Jain family whose roots trace back to Thirupanamoor, a village near Kanchipuram. His father, Simhakutty Varthaman, retired from the IAF as an Air Marshal, and his mother is a doctor. He grew up, in other words, inside the institution he would eventually come to represent. There was no epiphany, no sudden calling. There was simply a household where service was the family trade.The Sainik School yearsVarthaman was educated at Sainik School, a residential institution built specifically to feed India's National Defence Academy (NDA). Sainik Schools do not chase academic glamour. Their currency is discipline, physical endurance and an early, almost monastic exposure to hierarchy. Boys wake before dawn, drill, study, and are quietly sorted for a life that rewards obedience before it rewards individuality.Khadakwasla and the combat streamFrom Sainik School, Varthaman moved to the NDA in Khadakwasla, the tri-service academy that has fed the officer corps of the Indian Army, Navy and Air Force since 1954. He graduated into the combat, or fighter, stream of the IAF and was commissioned as a Flying Officer on 19 June 2004. What followed was years of technical training at IAF centres in Bathinda and Halwara, a apprenticeship on the Su-30 MKI before he was moved to the MiG-21 Bison squadron that would define his career. He was promoted Flight Lieutenant in 2006, Squadron Leader in 2010 and Wing Commander in 2017.The ninety seconds India remembersOn February 27, 2019, a day after the IAF struck a Jaish-e-Mohammed camp at Balakot, Varthaman was scrambled to intercept Pakistani fighters approaching the Line of Control. He shot down an F-16 before his MiG-21 Bison was struck by a missile, forcing him to eject into Pakistani territory. He was held for nearly 60 hours before being released on March 1, 2019. For his conduct that day, the government conferred on him the Vir Chakra, India's third highest wartime gallantry decoration, its citation praising his aggression despite what it called the enemy's immense numerical and technological superiority. He was promoted to Group Captain in December 2021.A new runwayVarthaman's move to Fly91 closes one chapter and opens a rather more prosaic one. It keeps him where his entire education pointed him from the age of eleven: in a cockpit. For a man built, quite literally, by an institution designed to manufacture composure under pressure, that continuity matters more than the uniform he is no longer wearing.Get the latest Education News and Live updates. articles.title: Horóscopo de hoy, jueves 3 de septiembre, de todos los signos del zodíaco: la jornada demanda atención y equilibrio entre responsabilidades y bienestar
articles.standfirst: La jornada invita a la reflexión y la toma de decisiones conscientes, priorizando el bienestar personal y relaciones armoniosas.
articles.summary: La jornada invita a la reflexión y la toma de decisiones conscientes, priorizando el bienestar personal y relaciones armoniosas.
articles.body: El horóscopo para hoy, jueves 3 de septiembre de 2026, marca una jornada donde las emociones y las relaciones interpersonales adquieren un papel protagónico. El clima astral sugiere que es un día adecuado para abordar situaciones que requieren apoyo mutuo y solidaridad, especialmente en el ámbito laboral y familiar. La energía general invitará a los individuos a mostrar empatía y comprensión, lo que podrá traducirse en momentos de conexión significativa con quienes les rodean. Durante la jornada, los temas más destacados serán el amor, las relaciones personales y el bienestar emocional. La necesidad de priorizar el autocuidado es evidente, pues muchos signos enfatizan la importancia de atender la salud física y mental. Asimismo, el trabajo y la creatividad se perfilan como áreas clave, donde se podrán encontrar oportunidades para hacer cambios significativos y desarrollar nuevos proyectos, aunque siempre con un enfoque cauteloso y reflexivo. Aprovechar este día para cultivar la comunicación efectiva y ser proactivo en la resolución de conflictos será fundamental. Es recomendable permitir que las nuevas ideas fluyan y prestar atención a las inquietudes de los demás, ya que la cooperación y la generosidad serán esenciales para sacar el máximo partido de las oportunidades que se presenten a lo largo de la jornada. Escucha más de lo que hablas y mide bien tus palabras: las formas importan. Busca aliados serenos y, si hace falta, utiliza canales formales para que quede constancia. No entres en provocaciones ni te expongas innecesariamente; apoya sin convertirte en el centro del conflicto. Al final del día, te sentirás mejor por haber estado a la altura y podría abrirse una vía para solucionarlo. Si mantienes la mente abierta y el corazón sereno, una conversación honesta te dará más claridad de la que esperabas. Evita las prisas y confía en tu intuición: bastará con ser tú mismo y cuidar los pequeños detalles. Cerrarás el día con la satisfacción de haber cumplido y con la ilusión renovada en lo sentimental. Traza una ruta clara, con hitos alcanzables y márgenes para los imprevistos y calibra bien los riesgos antes de dar cada paso. No está de más pedir una segunda opinión a alguien con experiencia y ser transparente con tus expectativas. Si ves señales de que conviene esperar, ajusta las velas sin miedo: un pequeño retraso hoy puede ahorrarte tempestades mañana. Mantén la cabeza fría, comunica con calma y avanza solo cuando sientas que el terreno es firme. Pon límites a las tareas y no te castigues si algo no sale perfecto a la primera: avanzar, aunque sea poco, también cuenta. Dedica unos minutos a algo que te guste —un paseo corto, música o un café con alguien— y notarás cómo cambia tu ánimo. Al final del día, date un pequeño premio y descansa bien; mañana verás todo con más claridad y energía renovada. También en el plano afectivo notarás más cercanía y comprensión; un gesto sencillo fortalecerá vínculos que dabas por rutinarios. En lo profesional, mantén abiertas las vías de diálogo: una colaboración inesperada puede convertirse en el impulso que necesitabas. Administra con sensatez tus recursos, pero date un pequeño capricho para celebrar los avances. Cuida tu descanso y no subestimes el poder de una pausa bien tomada. La armonía que siembres hoy regresará a ti multiplicada en los próximos días. Además, esa chispa de novedad te sacará de la rutina y te permitirá descubrir talentos que ni sabías que tenías. Acepta la invitación con mente abierta y buen humor: si tropiezas, te levantarás más fuerte. Al final del día, te llevarás una gran anécdota y, quizá, una nueva pasión. Escucha las señales de tu cuerpo y date el descanso que necesitas; pequeños ajustes en tu rutina, como hidratarte bien, moverte con suavidad y mantener una alimentación equilibrada, pueden marcar la diferencia. Un chequeo rápido despejará dudas y te dará la tranquilidad de estar haciendo lo correcto. No pospongas esa llamada: cuanto antes lo atiendas, antes recuperarás tu ritmo. Cuídate con cariño y verás cómo vuelves a sentirte con más energía para afrontar lo que venga. Prioriza solo lo esencial y no te sientas culpable por posponer lo que pueda esperar. Apaga notificaciones, respira profundo y date permiso para bajar el ritmo sin explicaciones. Un baño caliente, música suave o unos minutos de meditación te sentarán de maravilla. Evita tomar decisiones importantes hoy; con la mente despejada, mañana verás todo con más claridad y energía. Explícale que aprecias su interés, pero que tu tiempo es tuyo y necesitas administrarlo según tus prioridades. Marca límites claros sin dramatismos y sugiere alternativas solo si te nace compartir algún plan, dejando claro que la última palabra la tienes tú. Si insiste, toma distancia con amabilidad y ocupa tu agenda con lo que realmente te nutre. Recuperarás tu ritmo y tu paz y la relación, con límites sanos, también saldrá fortalecida. Empieza por informarte bien y conversar con la persona y con su equipo médico para asegurarte de que cualquier paso sea seguro y tenga sentido. No se trata de sustituir tratamientos, sino de sumar: desde grupos de apoyo y terapia psicológica, hasta ejercicio adaptado, educación en salud o prácticas de bienestar con respaldo profesional. Hazlo con tacto, sin imponer; propone, acompaña y respeta sus tiempos y decisiones. A veces el mayor apoyo es ayudar a organizar citas, gestionar trámites o, simplemente, estar presente y escuchar. Con pequeñas acciones constantes, puedes ser un puente hacia recursos que mejoren su calidad de vida. Organiza tus rutinas y establece prioridades para que el tiempo te rinda y evites saturarte. Planifica tus gastos con realismo y ahorra poco a poco para los imprevistos. Cuida tu descanso, aliméntate de forma equilibrada y reserva momentos para ti, porque el equilibrio también es productividad. Rodéate de personas que te inspiren, aprende de los errores sin castigarte y celebra cada pequeño avance. Con constancia y calma, verás cómo todo empieza a fluir. Evita también entrar en discusiones agotadoras o tomar decisiones importantes, porque el cansancio podría nublar tu juicio. Dedica el día a desconectar, ordenar un poco tu espacio, leer algo ligero o dar un paseo corto sin prisas. No te sientas culpable por posponer pendientes: hidrátate, come algo sencillo y date permiso para una buena siesta. Mañana, con la mente más clara, podrás retomar todo con mejor ánimo y mayor eficacia.

Four Democratic senators sent a letter Wednesday to Education Secretary Linda McMahon, calling for her to share details on how her department used $1 billion in funding intended for student loan administration.

The letter, authored by Sens. Cory Booker (D-N.J.), Jeff Merkley (D-Ore.), Chris Van Hollen (D-Md.) and Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.), questions why the Education Department has been “unable to meaningful alleviate the ongoing student loan default crisis” with its One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA) funding. The lawmakers shared the letter with The Hill

The tax and spending framework, which President Trump signed into law last year, afforded the Education Department $1 billion specifically for student aid administration in fiscal 2025.

But in its budget request from Congress for fiscal 2027, the department noted it had spent roughly $215.5 million of that funding as of the start of fiscal 2026 last October. The request also said more than $452.4 million of the $1 billion fund will remain unspent when the fiscal year ends on Sept. 30.

In their letter to McMahon, the four Democratic senators argued it was “unclear” how exactly her department spent that $215.5 million.

They went on to ask the Education Department to outline how it used the money — including whether it went toward paying student loan servicers, facilitating the interagency agreement it has with the Treasury Department or supporting its Federal Student Aid office’s “outreach” to borrowers in default or at risk of default.

The lawmakers requested McMahon provide these details by Sept. 16.

The Hill has reached out to an Education Department spokesperson for comment.

In the second quarter of 2026, 10.6 percent of student loan balances were delinquent — or at least 90 days past due, up from 10.3 percent in quarter one, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of New York’s quarterly report on household debt and credit.

Outstanding student loan debt stood at $1.65 trillion in the second quarter, per the New York Fed. The average federal student loan debt is $40,467 per borrower, according to the Education Data Initiative .

The Education Department made a slew of changes to the federal student loan repayment system under the OBBBA, including the addition of two new repayment plans.

Borrowers who take out loans after July 1 of this year must now repay the government via either using the Tiered Standard Plan (TSP) — which adjusts based on the amount of an individual’s principal balance, the interest rate on their loans and the length of their repayment period — or the Repayment Assistance Plan .

Borrowers who take out loans under the latter plan will make monthly payments based on their income and number of dependents.

The department is also phasing out the Biden-era Saving on a Valuable Education (SAVE) plan, which multiple federal judges halted in 2024 .

The more than 7.5 million borrowers still enrolled in the SAVE Plan must choose another avenue by Sept. 30, or else the department will automatically switch them to either the new tiered plan or the older Standard Repayment Plan.

Moving from the SAVE Plan to the Standard Repayment Plan will “dramatically raise monthly payments for borrowers” and put them “at an elevated risk of default,” the Democratic senators wrote to McMahon.

“Instead of making it a priority to lower costs for borrowers and alleviate the default crisis, the Trump administration has dedicated its energy to transferring student loan administration to the Treasury Department — a change that will do nothing to help borrowers, violates federal law, and only serves to advance the administration’s blatantly political crusade to dismantle [the Education Department],” the lawmakers wrote.

articles.title: America’s quiet socialist takeover is spreading from town halls to classrooms
articles.summary: Low-turnout school board elections in 2026 could let DSA chapters reshape curriculum and budgets before communities realize the lasting consequences.
articles.body: The socialist experiment in America is no longer confined to Washington or deep-blue national politics. It is coming to city halls and school boards across the country, where low-turnout elections can transform ambitious ideology into binding budgets and classroom policy. Local government often affects Americans’ everyday lives more directly than Washington, shaping taxes, municipal services, schools, policing, and housing. Americans should therefore pay close attention to the DSA’s steady advance into local government, where ideological commitments can collide with fiscal limits, practical administration, and community preferences. On affordability, New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s municipal grocery plan illustrates how a policy marketed as relief for working families can shift costs and risks onto others. New York City has allocated $70 million toward five municipal grocery stores that will be operated by private firms under city requirements while selling a defined basket of essential goods at prices the city says will be 30% below typical retail prices. That "basket of goods" applies to selected produce, meat, seafood, pantry staples and other goods—not necessarily every product in the stores. EXPERTS SCORCH MAMDANI'S GROCERY PLAN AS AN 'ILLUSION' THAT WILL HAVE TAXPAYERS FOOTING THE BILL The Multicultural Business Coalition, which says it represents hundreds of small, immigrant- and minority-owned grocers, has filed two lawsuits. The group wants to stop the plan, arguing that independent grocers operating on narrow margins cannot fairly compete against taxpayer-supported stores. The litigation has not established that businesses will close, and the first municipal store is not expected to open until next year. Nevertheless, the dispute exposes a recurring flaw in government-centered economic policy. Making goods cheaper for one group can impose costs on another, including on family-owned businesses, their employees, and taxpayers. A policy intended to protect the working class should not proceed without serious analysis of whether it could displace the middle-class entrepreneurs who have served these neighborhoods for decades. NYC BUSINESS OWNERS REVOLT OVER MAMDANI’S GOVERNMENT-RUN GROCERY STORES: ‘DOOMED FOR DISASTER' Local school boards present another opportunity for ideological politics because their decisions shape not only district budgets, but also what children are taught and which perspectives are treated as legitimate. When curriculum becomes a vehicle for political activism, academic achievement and intellectual diversity can become secondary. The concern is not that schools should ignore controversial subjects or disadvantaged students. It is that consequential policies can be adopted without adequately examining educational evidence, fiscal tradeoffs, dissenting perspectives, or the preferences of local families. Because school-board elections frequently receive limited public attention, organized political groups can exercise influence disproportionate to their support in the broader community. Los Angeles offers a prominent example. DSA-LA helped elect Karla Griego and Rocío Rivas to the Los Angeles Unified School District board and openly describes them as its "Socialists in Office." Its education agenda extends beyond conventional school policy to climate activism, immigration, LGBTQ+ protections, housing and labor policy, opposition to law enforcement, and anti-privatization efforts. Such politicization risks infringing on parental rights while losing sight of education’s fundamental responsibilities—ensuring students can read, handle basic arithmetic, think critically, and acquire the skills necessary to navigate adulthood. SOCIALISM MOVES INTO THE MAINSTREAM — THE WARNING SIGNS ARE ALL HERE Nor are these candidacies confined to Los Angeles. "DSA-LA has endorsed and campaigned for Estefany Castañeda, Rivas and Griego, all of whom won seats on Southern California education boards; San Diego DSA backed Erin Evans; Greater Baltimore DSA supports Baltimore school-board member Ashley ‘Ash’ Esposito; and in the 2026 election, Twin Cities DSA is supporting candidate Christin Crabtree in Minneapolis." The national organization has also encouraged chapters to recruit and run school-board candidates. Taken together, these campaigns show a deliberate effort to extend democratic-socialist influence into education governance. That makes transparency essential. School-board candidates should disclose organizational relationships, distinguish local educational needs from national political objectives, and explain how proposed policies will improve measurable student outcomes. Policymakers should likewise demand curriculum transparency, clear academic objectives, and credible evidence that new expenditures will improve outcomes such as literacy, followed by public reporting on whether those improvements materialize. America’s civic character will not be transformed only in Congress or the White House. It can change one municipal budget, ordinance, labor agreement, and curriculum decision at a time. But no movement’s moral certainty should exempt its proposals from fiscal arithmetic, educational evidence, viewpoint diversity, or community consent. The spread of DSA influence into local government is an effort to translate a national ideology into everyday governance, where the consequences become intensely personal. Spending commitments can raise taxes and crowd out essential services. Housing mandates can reshape neighborhoods. Public-safety experiments can affect whether residents feel secure. And ideological school policies can determine what children learn.
